evals.query: Set up a gRPC server in my Kora service that serves a UserService defined in a .proto file. Show me the dependencies and the handler.
expected_behavior: Uses the Kora 2.0 coordinates: platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:2.0.0.RC2") from mavenCentral(), io.koraframework:grpc-server, annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" (or ksp "io.koraframework:symbol-processors" for Kotlin)
Adds io.grpc:grpc-protobuf pinned to 1.84.0 and the com.google.protobuf Gradle plugin 0.10.0 with protoc 3.25.3 and protoc-gen-grpc-java 1.84.0
Registers build/generated/source/proto/main/grpc and .../main/java on the java source set (not kotlin.srcDir, even in a Kotlin project)
Extends io.koraframework.grpc.server.GrpcServerModule on the @KoraApp interface and boots with KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph)
Implements an UNTAGGED @Component that extends the generated UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceImplBase and uses io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver
Imports @Component from io.koraframework.common.annotation.Component
Never uses ru.tinkoff.kora, kora-parent, or a Kora 1.x package anywhere
Does not use field injection or non-Kora stereotype annotations (@GrpcService, @Service, @Autowired); uses constructor injection and @Component

evals.query: My Kora gRPC server tests fail with: java.lang.AbstractMethodError: does not define or inherit an implementation of the resolved method 'buildClientTransportServers(List, MetricRecorder)'. My build has testImplementation "io.grpc:grpc-inprocess:1.74.0". What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause as mixed io.grpc versions: grpc-inprocess is pinned at 1.74.0 while grpc-core arrives at 1.84.0 through io.koraframework:grpc-server
States that kora-bom constrains only io.koraframework:* artifacts and pins nothing under io.grpc, so every io.grpc coordinate is the application's responsibility
Fixes it by pinning grpc-inprocess (and every other io.grpc artifact, in both implementation and testImplementation) to 1.84.0
Notes that this fails at runtime rather than at compile time, and suggests auditing with ./gradlew dependencies filtered on io.grpc
Does not suggest excluding transitive dependencies, downgrading grpc-core, or adding a resolution strategy that forces the older version

evals.query: I bumped my Kora gRPC project to protoc 4.36.2 because that is the version in Kora's gradle/libs.versions.toml, and now the generated sources will not compile: "error: cannot find symbol @com.google.protobuf.Generated".
expected_behavior: Explains that io.grpc:grpc-protobuf:1.84.0 brings com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java:3.25.9, not the 4.x line
Explains that protoc 4.x gencode references com.google.protobuf.Generated and com.google.protobuf.RuntimeVersion, and that neither class exists in protobuf-java 3.25.9
States that kora-bom constrains only io.koraframework:* and pins nothing under com.google.protobuf, so the catalog value is not what reaches a consumer

Offers two consistent fixes: revert protoc to 3.25.3 (what all eight migrated Kora 2.0 gRPC projects pin), or keep protoc 4.36.2 and also add an explicit implementation "com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java:4.36.2"
Warns against mixing the two halves, and notes the runtime variant (NoClassDefFoundError: com/google/protobuf/RuntimeVersion) when 4.x is on the compile classpath but 3.x wins at runtime
Does not tell the user to just copy Kora's libs.versions.toml value, which works inside Kora's own build only because it pins protobuf-java alongside protoc
Identifies @Tag(GrpcServerModule.class) as the cause and says to remove the @Tag entirely

Explains that GrpcServerFactoryModule collects interceptors with an untagged All<ValueOf<ServerInterceptor>> claim (the @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) resolves to the factory module's own tag, which is null for GrpcServerModule), and that an untagged claim matches only untagged components
Notes that this fails silently: the build succeeds, the app starts, and only a test of the interceptor's observable effect catches it
States that the same rule applies to handlers: a @Tag on a *ImplBase @Component makes the RPC answer UNIMPLEMENTED
Does not invent a tag, a registration API, a priority annotation, or a serverBuilder override on a GrpcModule class

evals.query: Which interceptors does the Kora gRPC server register by default, and how do I customise the server builder?
expected_behavior: Names exactly one built-in: io.koraframework.grpc.server.interceptor.TelemetryInterceptor

States that the Kora 1.x names ContextServerInterceptor, CoroutineContextInjectInterceptor, MetricCollectorServerInterceptor and LoggingServerInterceptor do not exist in Kora 2.0, and neither does the GrpcModule class whose serverBuilder method 1.x told you to override
Explains that TelemetryInterceptor is added last and that gRPC runs interceptors in reverse order of addition, so it is the outermost one and user interceptors run inside its span

Describes the real customisation hooks on GrpcServerFactoryModule: an untagged ServerCredentials component for TLS, an untagged Configurer<ForwardingServerBuilder<?>> applied last before build(), or replacing the @DefaultComponent ForwardingServerBuilder outright
Does not reference foreign-framework interceptor APIs and does not invent a Kora ordering/priority mechanism

evals.query: Write the Kotlin gRPC handler for my Kora 2.0 service. I want createUser to be a suspend fun that calls my suspend repository, and getAllUsers to return a Flow<UserResponse>.
expected_behavior: Declines the suspend/Flow shape and explains that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous: suspend, Flow, Mono, Flux and CompletionStage are not Kora contracts
Writes plain override fun members extending the JAVA-generated UserServiceGrpc.UserServiceImplBase, using io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver
Explains that each call already runs on a virtual thread supplied by VirtualThreadExecutorTransportFilter, so blocking inside the handler is correct style
Notes that a suspend override produces "'createUser' overrides nothing", an error that never mentions coroutines
Implements the streaming method as void getAllUsers(request, StreamObserver<UserResponse>) with repeated onNext and a single onCompleted
Does not introduce runBlocking, Dispatchers.IO, GlobalScope, or protoc-gen-grpc-kotlin coroutine stubs as the solution
Does not claim Kora provides server-side grpc-kotlin coroutine service support
States that the Kora Context type was removed from the whole framework in Kora 2.0 and that no handler parameter of that type exists
Distinguishes it clearly from io.grpc.Context, which is gRPC's own unrelated type and still exists
Restores the handler signature to exactly what the generated stub declares: getUser(GetUserRequest, StreamObserver<UserResponse>)
Shows the interceptor writing to an io.grpc.Context.Key and propagating with io.grpc.Contexts.interceptCall(context, call, headers, next), and the handler reading it with KEY.get()
Mentions that MDC and the OpenTelemetry context are already bound per call as ScopedValues by the module, so logging is correlated without extra work
Does not suggest a Kora Context replacement class, a ThreadLocal that survives virtual-thread handoff, or a foreign-framework request-scope bean

evals.query: What metrics does the Kora gRPC server emit, how do I add custom tags, and why do I see nothing in Prometheus right now?
expected_behavior: Names rpc.server.call.duration as the only metric the module registers (a Micrometer Timer), tagged rpc.system.name, rpc.service, rpc.method, rpc.response.status_code (the status code name such as OK) and error.type

States that grpcServer.telemetry.metrics.enabled and grpcServer.telemetry.logging.enabled both default to FALSE in Kora 2.0, while tracing.enabled defaults to true, and that this is the reason nothing appears
Shows enabling it explicitly in the grpcServer.telemetry section, and notes that a MeterRegistry must also be in the graph (io.koraframework:micrometer-module)
Configures grpcServer.telemetry.metrics.tags for metric tags and grpcServer.telemetry.tracing.attributes for span attributes
Does not claim rpc.server.requests_per_rpc or rpc.server.responses_per_rpc exist in Kora 2.0
Does not claim metrics default to enabled, and does not suggest an actuator or a @Timed annotation as the mechanism

evals.query: Where do I set the gRPC port and turn on request logging for the Kora gRPC server?
expected_behavior: Configures the grpcServer section with port, and notes the default is 8090
Enables grpcServer.telemetry.logging.enabled = true and states that it defaults to false
Suggests externalizing the port via ${GRPC_PORT} or a literal plus a ${?GRPC_PORT} override
Mentions the request/response loggers io.koraframework.grpc.server.GrpcServer.request and .response, where DEBUG adds headers and TRACE adds protobuf bodies
Does not invent a foreign-framework server.port style property, and does not point at a netty section — Kora 2.0 serves gRPC over OkHttp

evals.query: I set grpcServer.reflectionEnabled = true but grpcurl still answers UNIMPLEMENTED against my Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Identifies the missing io.grpc:grpc-services dependency as the cause
Explains that the module probes for io.grpc.protobuf.services.ProtoReflectionServiceV1 with a classpath check and ignores the flag with no warning when the class is absent
Adds io.grpc:grpc-services pinned to 1.84.0, matching every other io.grpc artifact
Shows a grpcurl list command and notes that the full method name uses the .proto package, not java_package
Recommends keeping reflection off in production unless the endpoint is internal only

evals.query: Add a server-streaming RPC GetAllUsers and a client-streaming RPC CreateUsers to my Kora gRPC handler, in Java and in Kotlin.
expected_behavior: Declares both rpcs with the stream keyword in the .proto contract
Server streaming: void getAllUsers(Empty, StreamObserver<UserResponse>) emitting multiple onNext then exactly one onCompleted
Client streaming: returns StreamObserver<CreateUserRequest> that accumulates values in onNext and replies in onCompleted
Explains that onError on the returned request observer is an inbound notification that the call already ended, not a place to send a response
Uses the same io.grpc.stub.StreamObserver shapes in Kotlin, extending the Java-generated *ImplBase, with no suspend and no Flow
Keeps business logic in an injected service component, not in the generated protobuf types
Does not introduce reactive or coroutine streaming abstractions

evals.query: Add API key authentication to my Kora 2.0 gRPC server by checking the authorization metadata header, but only for UserStreamingService.
expected_behavior: Implements io.grpc.ServerInterceptor as an UNTAGGED @Component from io.koraframework.common.annotation so GrpcServerFactoryModule discovers it
Scopes it by comparing UserStreamingServiceGrpc.SERVICE_NAME against call.getMethodDescriptor().getServiceName() and passing other services straight through, because every interceptor is global
Reads the header via Metadata.Key.of("authorization", Metadata.ASCII_STRING_MARSHALLER)
Rejects with call.close(Status.UNAUTHENTICATED, new Metadata()) AND returns an empty ServerCall.Listener

Reads the expected key from a typed @ConfigSource interface (io.koraframework.config.common.annotation.ConfigSource) injected through the constructor, not from a @ConfigSource-annotated constructor parameter
Does not use a servlet filter or a foreign-framework security chain

evals.query: My gRPC handler should return a proper not-found error when the user does not exist instead of a generic failure.
expected_behavior: Uses io.grpc.Status.NOT_FOUND with withDescription(...).asRuntimeException()
Sends it through responseObserver.onError(...) or throws the StatusRuntimeException
Explains that exactly one terminal signal (onError or onCompleted) must be sent per RPC and never onNext afterwards
Notes that withCause attaches the cause server-side only and never reaches the client, so client-facing detail belongs in the description or in trailers
Stays gRPC-native with io.grpc.Status; does not map to an HTTP status code, an HttpServerResponseException, or a foreign-framework response wrapper

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 gRPC server logs requests at DEBUG, and clients send an x-api-key metadata header that now shows up in the logs. We also want TRACE bodies for debugging but the messages contain passport numbers. How do we mask both?
expected_behavior: Adds x-api-key to grpcServer.telemetry.logging.maskHeaders and restates the defaults authorization, cookie, set-cookie, because a configured list replaces the default
Explains that masked values are replaced by the @Tag(GrpcServerTelemetry.class) MaskingStrategy component (default ***), which can be replaced, e.g. with MaskingKeepLast
States that there is no mask config key

Explains that protobuf bodies are logged at TRACE via DefaultGrpcServerBodyConverter with no masking, and that redaction means providing a DefaultGrpcServerBodyConverter subclass (overriding convertRequestMessage/convertResponseMessage or convertMessage) from a factory method typed DefaultGrpcServerBodyConverter
Points to kora-aop-logging for the shared masking model
anti_behavior: Claims gRPC bodies are masked by a DataMasker or by maskHeaders
Writes a ServerInterceptor that strips the header before telemetry as the masking mechanism
Invents keys such as maskBody, mask or maskMetadata
